steps: Plan the location

Allow for ember protection, clearances and a chimney path that avoids cutting joists; check the floor for approx. 500lbs plus venting. Minimum 84" from the base of the unit to the ceiling, inside the chase and in the room.

Fireplace system weight (floor check)approx. 500lbs(227Kg), plus the venting
Maker's website: Weight 626 lb.
  • Combustible floor or raised base both allowed; add the base height to all measurements if raising the unit.
  • Chimney should penetrate the highest part of the roof, stay clear of roof offsets, trees and obstructions, and use the fewest offsets possible.
  • Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance. Not tested for installation into a factory built fireplace.
  • Manufactured/mobile homes: not in a sleeping room. U.S.: per HUD Manufactured Home Construction and Safety. Canada: access openings into the enclosure for inspection, with covers that need a household tool.
  • No makeshift or temporary installs. A WETT (Canada) or HEARTH (U.S.A.) certified installer is strongly recommended.

Uncrating (p. 16): remove the wood top and supports, then the 4 screws securing the fireplace to the pallet.
Frame the chase

Frame to the minimum dimensions in Figures 9-10 (diagrams) with the required steel stud framing kit, and no wood framing directly in front of the chimney system at the top front. Keep insulation off the unit and leave the space above it open.

Framing dimensions appear only as diagrams on this page. They are minimums to combustibles: enlarge them for any drywall/wallboard inside the enclosure, since drywall is combustible.

  • Insulated chase: cover the insulation with drywall or non-combustible panels; the fireplace must not touch insulation or loose filling.
  • Do not insulate the front portion of the chase above the unit.
  • No recess, shelves or cupboards above the fireplace and nothing inside the minimum chase area: the open volume is needed for heat management.
Set the unit + framing kit

Push the fireplace in with the casing flush to the front framing and secure it per local code. Set the assembled steel framing kit on top, legs down and flush with the front, screw the outer legs into the unit and fasten the kit to the chase framing.

1. Assemble kit 80000181 on a flat surface: Teks #8 x 1/2" screws fix the legs to the bottom stud, the center supports to the bottom stud, then the top stud to the center supports.
  2. Push the fireplace into place, casing flush with the front framing; secure as required by local code.
  3. Place the kit on the unit, legs down, front edge flush with the fireplace front; screw through the outer legs into the unit using the holes provided.
  4. Align fireplace and steel framing flush with the chase (the outer non-combustible board needs a flat surface) and fasten the kit to the chase framing.
Install the chimney

Listed 6" chimney (UL 103HT in the U.S., CAN-ULC S629 in Canada) on the chimney maker's fireplace anchor plate, with a firestop/radiation shield at every floor or wall. Outlet at least 15ft above the base of the unit; support lengths over 15'.

1. Plumb up from the flue collar; cut and frame square holes through floors, ceilings and roof; mount the chimney maker's firestops and radiation shields.
  2. Keep the chimney maker's clearances; never fill the space with insulation or other combustibles; fit insulation shields where required.
  3. Insert the anchor/base plate into the flue collar, seal with stove cement, secure with stainless steel screws (anchor plate spacer #11220002 if it won't sit flush).
  4. Stack sections so the chimney rests on the anchor plate; avoid joints between ceiling and roof; secure each connection with three (3) #8x½" stainless screws.
  5. Fit the roof radiation shield, flashing and storm collar; keep the vapour barrier sealed.
  6. More than 5'(1.5m) above the roof: brace it. Attach the rain cap and check the flashing for leaks.

Offsets: max four 30° elbows (U.S.A.) or four 45° elbows (Canada); min 36"(915mm) of chimney before the first elbow; offset lengths to a maximum of 4ft. (1.22m); support per the chimney maker, and after the first 15' (4.5m).
Combustion air

For outside air, connect 4" rigid or flex pipe to the outside air adapter (factory-installed on the right, swappable to the left) and an approved 4" inlet vent cap at least 5ft below the chimney outlet. Otherwise the fireplace draws room air.

• Outside air must come from outdoors; never terminate in an attic space or garage. Secure the fireplace to the structure so the duct can't dislodge.
  • Hole in the closest exterior wall or in the floor inside the chase; cover with 20GA wire mesh minimum rodent screen; water protection per code. Insulated flex recommended in cold climates.
  • Room air: through a space between the surround panels or air inlet ducts near the floor in the chase. Keep the living space well ventilated; negative pressure can pull fumes into the room.

Consult local code or CAN/CSA-B365 before proceeding.
Wire the blowers

Bring Romex 14/2 (or equivalent) through the cable clamp on the right side of the support base to the terminal strip, fed from a wall switch or fan speed controller (not supplied) on 120 VAC. Use a certified/licensed electrician.

Blower rating115 V, 60 Hz, 1.1A

Connect as shown in the wiring diagram (Figure 19). Local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 in the U.S. and CSA C22.2 in Canada.
Remote heat kit (optional)
One or two kits: open a top knockout, fit the backflow damper and duct adapter, and run 6" listed B-vent (20ft. max effective run) to the wall blower box. Each kit needs a 30in² chase air inlet.

1. Remove a top knockout panel per kit and cut out the insulation below it, down to the next opening.
  2. Place the backflow damper (flap free, normally closed with the blower off); fit the duct adapter over it and secure both to the outer casing with 4 screws.
  3. Mount the remote blower box to the framing by its tabs, every edge of the casing/outlet grill at least 12"(305mm) from the ceiling or side walls and 36"(914mm) from the floor.
  4. Attach the 10" x 3 1/4" transition boot with aluminium duct tape; run 6" Type B flexible or rigid gas vent (not included) to the fireplace, screwed and foil-taped; firestops through walls and floors.
  5. Wire the kit blower (120V, 60HZ, 80 watts), best on its own switch or speed controller in the room the outlet is in.
  6. Drywall must not cover the blower opening: remove the face plate, butt the drywall to the casing edges, refit the face plate and outlet grill; fit inlet grills after decorative finishing.
Note: the remote heat kit's part number is printed as WODC.RHKIT in the kit instructions on p. 24 and as WODC.RHKA on the rating label on p. 45; the parts list on p. 46 shows Remote Heat Duct kit 11490003.
Facing, hearth + ember protection

Cover the front only with non-combustible cement board (bottom to 7ft., 60" wide), never past the built-in 1/2" facing edge/stop. Build any raised hearth from non-combustibles, then fit the 2" metal safety strip and the ember protection.

• Cement board from the bottom of the fireplace to 7ft. (2.13m), 60" (1.524m) wide, centered; finish joints per the board maker. If possible, leave the 31" x 12 1/2" area above the door unfastened so the fireplace can expand and contract.
  • Non-combustible finishes only within 10" of the door's outer edge, under the door to the floor, and 16" above the heat exchanger's air deflector.
  • Raised hearth: non-combustible materials and framing, no higher than 9 3/8" from the bottom of the unit.
  • Safety strip: 2" (50mm) deep metal, unit width, half under the fireplace front and half under the hearth extension; seal the gap with non-combustible material such as sand-cement grout.
  • Ember protection and combustible mantels: see the Ember protection and Mantel specs.

FP30 AR LE with the Craftsman surround: follow the Craftsman section instead.
Install the firebricks
With the unit upright: 9 full-size (A) and 1 cut (C) on the floor, 4 full-size at the rear, then 3 full-size and 1 cut (B) on each side. 19 full-size and 3 cut bricks in all.

A · 9" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"5096.99
B · 9" X 3 1/2" X 1 1/4"3245.501
C · 7 1/4" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"245.001
Firebrick set80000086

Burn directly on the bricks; no grates or andirons. Replace broken or missing bricks.
Craftsman surround (AR LE only)

Remove the upper and lower grills (not reused), mount the side brackets and trace the top brow, then board the front with non-combustible board (84" high, 60" wide). Fit the top brow and upper grill, the lower grill, then the front.

Fits only the FP30 AR LE; its clearances and chase inlet rules supersede the main manual. Requires a chase air inlet: 16 sq.in. min, no higher than 12" from the bottom of the fireplace. Raised hearth max 7".

  1. Remove the upper and lower louver assemblies (5/16" nut driver).
  2. Side brackets: drill out the top rivet with the 7/32" bit, align the bracket over the two remaining rivet heads, start one 1/4-20 thread cutting screw, then (5) #8 self-drilling screws; tighten gently. Repeat on the other side.
  3. Dry-fit the top brow mount in the bracket cutouts, trace its top edge, set it aside.
  4. Non-combustible board with the arch template cutout; no vertical joints above the unit; keep the brow pencil line visible. Max 5/8" total thickness in the dashed area by and below the side brackets.
  5. Fit the top brow mount, then the upper grill with three (3) #8 self drilling screws; fill board joints.
  6. Lower grill: loosen the two ash shelf bolts (3/8" socket; the shelf is heavy, don't remove the bolts), pass the air control lever through the grill slot, hook the grill slots over the screw heads, retighten.
  7. Front: lever through the lower opening, tilt up under the brow, guide the side tabs into the bracket slots until it drops and locks; fix with the four black #8 Torx screws behind the front (lift the door off its hinge side for access).

The surround must be removed to reach the rating label.

light.title: Starting a fire
light.html:
Start with newspaper, dry kindling and dry wood only. Never use gasoline, lighter fluid, kerosene or any other liquid to start or freshen a fire.

  1. Move the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the center of the firebox. Crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it, then add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully in flames. Stay with the fireplace while the door is open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. When there is a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air control for normal burning.

Burn right on the firebricks. Don't use a grate or andirons to raise the wood.

Your first 2-3 fires cure the paint, which gives off smoke and a smell. Open all windows and doors. Small children, older adults and anyone with breathing problems should leave the area during these hot burns. Smoke detectors may go off more often at first. Don't disconnect them.

burn.title: Air control, reloading & overnight burns
burn.html:
The air control sets how hard the fire burns. High is all the way to the left. Every home is different, so find the setting that suits yours by trial and error, and note it for next time.

Reloading

  1. Move the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. This stops smoke puffing out and flames rolling out.
  3. Load dry logs of different shapes and sizes (18" long is recommended), placed so air can flow between them. Don't load wood where it could fall out when you open the door.
  4. For the cleanest burn, add two or three logs (or half a load) at a time and leave the air fairly wide open. After 15 to 30 minutes you can turn it down a lot.
Smoke pouring down the glass means you turned the air down too soon or set it too low.

Overnight burns

Use unsplit logs, and char them completely on High before you set the air control to Low. To restart, rake the hot embers to the front, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to High. Once the wood has charred, reset the control.

Keep the door closed while burning. Use High only to start a fire or heat up a fresh load. The low burn setting is set at the factory and must not be altered.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
This fireplace is designed to burn natural cordwood only. Dry, seasoned wood burns cleaner and more efficiently. Wet wood smolders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out.

  • Air-dry (season) wood for six months or more. Store it under cover, away from flames and heat.
  • Denser, heavier wood gives more heat, which is why hardwoods are preferred.
  • Maximum log length is 20 inches; 18 inches is ideal.

Test your wood

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. If it burns on more than one side within one minute, it's dry. If it turns black and lights within three minutes, it's damp. If it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes, it's soaked. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Wet, green, unseasoned or treated wood, salt-water wood, coal or charcoal, garbage, lawn clippings and yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything with plastic, rubber (including tires) or asbestos, cardboard and paper products, plywood, particleboard, construction or demolition debris, solvents, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products. Burning any of these may release toxic fumes, or make the heater ineffective and cause excessive smoke. Salt-water wood, garbage, solvents and anything with plastic contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty. Charcoal can make deadly carbon monoxide, and you should never barbecue in the fireplace. Paper, sawdust or wax fire starters are fine for lighting.

Don't store wood within the fireplace's clearances, in front of it or under it.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out only when the fireplace is cold.

  1. When ashes are 3 to 4 inches deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, remove the extra ash.
  2. Leave a bed of ash about 1" deep on the firebox floor. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed for the next fire.
  3. Keep the inside front of the firebox clear of heavy ash. That is where boost air comes in.

Getting rid of ashes

  • Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  • Set the closed container outside, on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  • If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder is completely cool.
  • Don't put other trash in the ash container.
Remove ashes often. Embers can roll out the door and start a fire.

glass.title: Glass & door gasket
glass.html:
Clean the glass with fireplace glass cleaner, and only when the fireplace is cold. Never use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that could scratch it.

What the glass tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good burning and dry wood. A black, greasy film that is hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. The same deposit is building up in your chimney just as fast.

Protect the glass

  • Don't slam the door or hit the glass. Before you close the door, make sure no log sticks out far enough to hit it.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the fireplace again. Use only 21-5/8" x 11-3/8" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer, never another material.

Door gasket

The door seals with a 5/8" fiberglass rope gasket that needs only light pressure. Check it weekly for sagging, damage or slipping out of place, and replace it when needed.

Parts to ask your dealer for: door gasket 80000179, glass gasket 80000182, replacement glass 80000183. The door assembly differs by model: 80000180 (FP30 LE) or 80000805 (FP30 Arch).

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Burning wood slowly makes tar and vapors that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If creosote catches fire it burns extremely hot, so it has to be removed before it builds up.

Keep it clean

  • Inspect and clean the chimney system at the start of each burning season, before your first fire. Remove and check the rain cap.
  • Check daily for creosote until experience shows how often you need to clean.
  • Avoid very hot fires that can start a chimney fire: household trash, cardboard, Christmas tree branches, or a full load on hot coals with the air open for a long time.
Note: p. 5 says to inspect and clean your chimney system at least every two months during the burning season; p. 8 says to inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least twice a year during the heating season.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the chimney top, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get everyone ready to leave, and meet at an agreed place outside.
  2. Close the air control on the fireplace.
  3. Call the fire department. Keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for damage and cracks. A certified installer is strongly recommended.

overfire.title: Over-firing & draft
overfire.html:
Do not over-fire the fireplace. Over-firing means trying to get more heat than it is designed for. It can permanently damage the fireplace and chimney and shortens its life. Leaving it uncorrected can be hazardous and may void the warranty.

What causes it

  • Burning with the door open.
  • Too much chimney draft.
  • Damaged door gaskets letting extra air into the firebox.
  • Burning kiln-dried lumber, mill ends or paper waste.
  • Running on a high setting for long stretches.

Reading the draft

Draft is the pull that moves air from the fireplace up the chimney. It depends on the chimney's length, the local terrain and nearby obstructions.

  • Too much draft: a fire you can't control, or a fireplace part or the chimney glowing red.
  • Too little draft: smoke puffing back into the room, or smoke leaking out at the fireplace or chimney joints.
Use High only to start a fire or heat up a fresh load, then turn the air control back down once the wood has charred.

care.title: Weekly & monthly checks
care.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and too much warping.

Weekly

  • Firebricks: check for cracks.
  • Door gasket: sagging, out of place or damaged.

Monthly

  • Brick rails and their tabs.
  • The air riser tube at the back of the firebox.
  • The back of the airwash chamber.
  • The baffle locking pin and the boost manifold cover.

When the chimney is cleaned

Check the top baffle board or blanket, the baffle and its gasket, the top heat shield and its bolt, the brick rails and the manifold. A little baffle warping (up to 1/4") is normal. Replace the baffle if it is warped more than 1/4" or cracked. Take the baffle out only for chimney cleaning, never burn with it or its insulation removed, and cover the top of the baffle air tube while it is out.

Found damage? Contact your dealer. Burning with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty. Replace broken or missing firebricks.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
• Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended near the fireplace. Never disconnect them.
  • The fireplace is hot while it is burning. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Touching it can burn skin.
  • Keep furniture, drapes and anything else that can burn at least 48" from the door. Keep the area clear of newspapers and clutter.
  • Always burn with the door closed. An open door can throw sparks and pull too much air out of the room.
  • Never use gasoline, kerosene, lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen a fire. Keep them well away while the fireplace is in use.
  • Don't store wood within the clearances, in front of the fireplace or under it.
  • Make sure everyone who runs the fireplace knows how, including what to do in a chimney fire.
  • Never put an unvented gas log set or a fireplace insert in this fireplace.
If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the fireplace again.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (heat breakage, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 years from purchase, parts and laborAny defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets.
  • Labor under the lifetime coverage. Firebox rails and heat shields are not part of it.
  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accidents, lack of maintenance or modification.

Over-firing, excessive draft, heating too large an area, and fuel with high sodium content, plastics or chemicals may void it.

Making a claim

Contact your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. The serial number is on the cover of this manual and on the rating label, which pulls out by a small tab from under the ash lip, just below the bottom louver. A Craftsman surround has to come off first. You can register online at pacificenergy.net/register.

This is a summary. The full terms are in the manual.

specFrame.title: Facing & finishing clearances
specFrame.html:
Front facingNon-combustible cement board only, then non-combustible finish
Board coverageBottom of fireplace to 7ft. (2.13m), 49" above the top finishing edge; 60" (1.524m) wide, centered
Facing edge/stopBuilt-in, 1/2" (13mm) deep; no board or finish beyond/inside it
Leave unfastened if possible31" (785mm) x 12 1/2" (320mm) area above the door
Non-combustible only10" [255mm] out from the outer edge of the door; under the door to the floor; min 16" [405mm] above the heat exchanger's air deflector
Mantel side facing (max 4" deep)10" (255mm) from side of door

Material inside the facing edge/stop blocks airflow into the blowers and overheats the fireplace and blowers; that is not covered under warranty. Framing: the steel stud framing kit must be used; minimum framing dimensions are shown only as diagrams (Figures 9-10) on p. 17. Drywall is combustible, so allow for its thickness. Keep insulation off the unit, don't insulate the chase front above it, and build no recess, shelves or cupboards above it.

specAir.title: Combustion & chase air
specAir.html:
Outside air duct4"(102mm) rigid or flex; insulated flex recommended in cold climates
AdapterFactory-installed on the right side; can swap with the left cover plate; draw from side or back
Inlet capApproved 4"(102mm) inlet vent cap, 20GA wire mesh minimum rodent screen
Inlet locationAt least 5ft (1.5m) below the chimney outlet; never in an attic space or garage
Chase air inlet (FP30 LE, FP30 AR LE)30in² (194 cm²) per remote heat kit; two may combine to 60in² (387 cm2); 1 1/2" (40mm) to 18" (460mm) off the floor
Chase air inlet (AR LE + Craftsman)16 sq.in. [100cm2] required, no higher than 12" [305mm] from the bottom of the fireplace

Room air is the alternative: through a space between the surround panels or air inlet ducts near the floor in the chase. With outside air, secure the fireplace to the structure so the duct can't dislodge. Consult local code or CAN/CSA-B365. Chase inlets must draw from the room the fireplace is in. Without a remote heat kit a chase inlet is not required, but a single inlet is recommended for efficiency.

Note: without a remote heat kit, p. 24 says a 30in2 chase inlet is required "if the chase has vent openings or is open in any way"; p. 29 says one is required "if the chase has any vents or openings above the height of the door".

specElec.title: Blowers & electrical
specElec.html:
Blower electrical rating115 V, 60 Hz, 1.1A
Supply120 VAC household electrical system
WireRomex 14/2 or equivalent, through the cable clamp on the right-hand side of the support base
ControlWall switch or fan speed controller (not supplied)
Remote heat kit blower120V, 60HZ, 80 watts

Certified/licensed electrician; local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 (U.S.) / CSA C22.2 (Canada). The two blowers sit in the bottom compartment: disconnect power, remove the bricks and the 8 access-panel bolts (7/16" socket), slide the thermo switch bracket back, lift out the two-piece lower panel, disconnect the blower leads at the terminal block, remove the 2 wingnuts and lift the blower out. Parts: blower assembly RHS 80000168 / LHS 80000169; blower only right 80000904 / left 80000905; blower thermo switch 80001814; access panel gasket 80001678 (replace it if it isn't in good condition).

The manual also prints the access panel gasket as pn.# 800001678 (p. 14); its parts list gives Access Cover Gasket 80001678 (p. 46).

conflicts.issue: Heat output range: the efficiency table gives EPA BTU output 13,700 to 65,650 Btu/hr; the text on the same page says the heater delivers 14,600 to 38,600 Btu/hr under specific test conditions.
conflicts.reason: Two separately defined figures on p. 3, each with its own stated basis: the table's EPA BTU output (13,700 to 65,650 Btu/hr) is based on CSA B415 efficiency and the burn rates from the low and high EPA tests using Douglas Fir dimensional lumber (footnote 3); the text gives 14,600 to 38,600 Btu/hr as the heat delivered under specific test conditions. The drawer now states both with their bases.

conflicts.issue: U.S. ember protection depth: 19 1/8" from the front (U.S. only, p. 31) vs 18" (457 mm) with no country split in the clearance table (p. 16) and rating label (p. 45); the Craftsman table also gives 18" (460mm) (p. 35).

Maximum chimney height reference: recommended maximum 35' (10.7 m) from the top of the fireplace to the rain cap (p. 16) vs a 15ft minimum measured from the base of the unit 'up to a maximum height of 35' (10.7m)' (p. 19).
Chimney inspection interval: at least every two months during the burning season (p. 5) vs at least twice a year during the heating season (p. 8).
Remote heat kit part number: WODC.RHKIT (p. 24) vs WODC.RHKA on the rating label (p. 45); parts list shows Remote Heat Duct kit 11490003 (p. 46).
Access panel gasket part number: pn.# 800001678 (p. 14) vs Access Cover Gasket 80001678 in the parts list (p. 46).

When a 30in2 chase inlet is required without a remote heat kit: 'if the chase has vent openings or is open in any way' (p. 24) vs 'if the chase has any vents or openings above the height of the door' (p. 29).

review.notes: One manual (100004186) covers both catalog models (FP30 LE and FP30 AR LE / Arch) with a single efficiency table, one dimension figure ('FP30 & FP 30 Arch') and one clearance table, so most numbers are shared. Model-specific content: the Craftsman surround fits the FP30 AR LE only and supersedes the main-manual clearances (side wall 29", mantel heights, raised hearth 7", chase inlet 16 sq.in.); these are given as separate rows. Arch-specific door, louvre and ash shelf part numbers are on p. 46; the manual lists one replacement glass size and part (80000183) for both doors. Diagram-only content not transcribed: overall dimensions (Figure 8, p. 16), framing dimensions (Figures 9-10, p. 17), masonry chimney figure values (p. 21), remote heat duct options (p. 25), Craftsman board cutout (p. 38), ember protection drawings (p. 31; text values used). Framing kit item quantities on p. 18 are ambiguous in the text layout and were left out. Manual metric typos not reproduced: 6" mantel depth printed '(159 mm)' (p. 33); firebrick B '9" X 3 1/2" X 1 1/4" (102 mm x 115 mm x 32 mm)' (p. 34). The Craftsman 11" mantel height is printed '58” 3/4”' (p. 36) and given as 58 3/4" (check_numbers flags '58 3/4' for this reason only). Mantel column C (height above the convection outlet grill) is printed only on the 6/8/10/12" rows (p. 33). The rating label (p. 45) gives ember protection 'to side of unit 8 in.' while p. 16 says 8" from the side of the door opening in the U.S.A. Warranty page p. 48 carries footer revision 060624 (rest 071124); pp. 49-51 are blank 'Operator Instructions' pages. Not in the manual, so left out: owner blower operation, blower cfm, power outages, firebox volume, heating area, viewing/glass area, non-catalytic designation. Oct 12 update (report everything): the seven conflict boxes became reader notes (5 substantive, 1 clerical, 1 not_a_conflict). Website notes: specPerf (Heat Output (Cord Wood) 99,000 BTU after the EPA BTU output row; Log Size (recommended) 16" after the ideal wood length row) and step0 (Weight 626 lb., after a new row giving the manual's approx. 500lbs(227Kg) plus the venting, p. 15). website.json prints no 65,600 BTU figure (the catalog's btu_output_max); the website's only heat output row is the 99,000 BTU cord wood figure, so that is what the specPerf note quotes. Website rows the manual does not cover were skipped: firebox size 3.0 cu.ft., glass viewing area 246 sq.in., 2x80 cfm blowers, north-south fuel loading, the U.S. availability banner.
